u0724.gist: PM Modi completed 25 continuous years heading a government (Gujarat CM from October 7, 2001, then PM in 2014) on October 7, 2026.
facts: June 10, 2026: became longest-serving elected PM for consecutive terms, surpassing Jawaharlal Nehru.
Nehru first took oath as elected PM on May 13, 1952 and served until May 27, 1964.
Modi's continuous PM tenure, May 26, 2014 to June 10, 2026: 4399 days.
March 22, 2026: longest-serving head of an elected government (CM + PM combined): 8,931 days.
Uzbekistan's 'Oliy Darajali Do'stlik' Order (Order of Highest Friendship) from President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, August 30, 2026.
2026 honours: Indonesia's Bintang Adipurna, Seychelles' Guardian of the Blue Horizon (first time given), FAO's Agricola Medal.
Also: Royal Norwegian Order of Merit, Sweden's Royal Order of the Polar Star, Israel's Medal of the Knesset.
u0724.hook: Award-country pairs: Bintang Adipurna = Indonesia; Blue Horizon = Seychelles; White Double Cross = Slovakia; Polar Star = Sweden; Knesset = Israel; Nishan = Ethiopia; Agricola = FAO.
u0724.trap: Two different records: 4399 days = continuous PM tenure; 8,931 days = CM + PM tenure combined.

mcq.why: Seychelles gave 'Guardian of the Blue Horizon' on June 28, 2026; first time bestowed.

mcq.q: On June 10, 2026, PM Narendra Modi became the longest-serving elected PM for consecutive terms, surpassing the record of:
mcq.why: He passed Nehru, elected PM from May 13, 1952 to May 27, 1964.
